every action request can consume the capacity the selected content was meant
to save. Selection, active residency, semantic construction, action
expression, verification, and closure remain separate boundaries.

The two newest large-world source-navigation studies then tested that boundary
on one broad authentic research task with Q3 XL, a sister package rather than
the Qwen3.8 package. The predecessor held only the standing task, current exact
objects, and the latest literal action/result frontier. Both sealed seeds spent
all 32 calls in repeated root/candidate-tree orientation, read zero exact atlas
documents or sections, mutated nothing, ran no check, and never submitted.
Their own searches returned usable exact source identities, but each result
disappeared after the next non-search action; exposure across separate pages did
not become a durable selected set. The [predecessor results](experiments/large-world-source-navigation-v0/runs/2026-08-18-sealed-bank-v0/RESULTS.md)
and [direct transcript audit](experiments/large-world-source-navigation-v0/runs/2026-08-18-sealed-bank-v0/DIRECT_TRANSCRIPT_AUDIT.md)
identify cumulative navigation state, not passive action basis or semantic
selection, as the missing interface.

The matched successor retained exact, deduplicated atlas pages and search
results as current navigation objects. Both actors then traversed all four root
pages once, descended into studies, read seven exact evidence documents across
six experiment directories, and repeated no navigation operation. Neither
produced an artifact: seed 42 used all 32 calls, spending 11 reopening already
acquired receipts after explicitly budgeting the remaining calls for writing,
checking, and submission; seed 314159 formed a substantially correct cross-source
synthesis by turn 18 but stopped before call 23 when its projected prompt plus
the frozen completion allowance exceeded the context limit by 320 tokens. The
[successor results](experiments/large-world-navigation-continuity-v0/runs/2026-08-18-sealed-bank-v0/RESULTS.md)
and [direct transcript audit](experiments/large-world-navigation-continuity-v0/runs/2026-08-18-sealed-bank-v0/DIRECT_TRANSCRIPT_AUDIT.md)
therefore separate three boundaries: cumulative mechanical navigation state
was a real missing interface; after that repair, Q3 XL assembled a useful but
task-incomplete evidence set; and the remaining horizon was lost through
acquisition-stopping/call-budget organization in one seed and combined prompt
capacity in the other. Exact reads here were not all decision-necessary merely
because requested: the successor's reopen churn shows that previously read
sources can collapse as new large documents arrive, making reacquisition a
working-set effect rather than evidence of semantic selection failure.

This pair does not promote an atlas, controller, commit gate, semantic
summary, memory, action basis, eviction policy, or automatic phase boundary.
It also does not convert successful traversal into a successful artifact result:
no memo was constructed, checked, repaired, or closed in either run. The
demonstrated capability is bounded navigation and selection under retained
mechanical continuity; the unresolved runtime design is global prompt-capacity
accounting across resident navigation and exact-content regions, plus whether a
feasible acquisition/construction schedule can be organized inside a frozen call
allowance. Independent regional byte caps did not compose into a safe total
prompt, so the next worthwhile authentic question is whether naturally arising
research, writing, or repository-scale tasks with a feasible action budget
reproduce this breadth-versus-construction boundary under one global rendered-
prompt budget—without rerunning either seed, raising the cap, or tuning another
evidence-churn policy around these trajectories.

## Design consequences

The laboratory should represent, custody, and test these objects separately:

| Object | Semantic owner in an experiment | What custody may validate |
|---|---|---|
| Artifact unit | Fixture/task author, or a separately tested model step | ID, exact bytes/range, version, provenance |
| Evidence binding | Task author control or model treatment | declared IDs, exact source bytes, proposal provenance |
| Supporting subspan | Optional model treatment only when a task requires a pinpoint | parent record, exact byte range/text, version, provenance |
| Active obligation | Task author control or model/role treatment | exact task ID/text/span, selection provenance |
| Executable predicate | Task author or independently reviewed adapter | exact setup/operation/observation/criterion bytes, execution result, candidate identity; never unexecuted sibling truth |
| Complete task audit | Task author or independently reviewed adapter | declared coverage of written requirements, complete predicate inventory, exact expected/observed results, candidate identity, and currentness; never a semantic readiness claim |
| Passing sibling control | Task author-selected experimental contrast over independently executed predicates | exact sibling program/result and candidate identity; no claim that the model must preserve it |
| Temporal trace | Task-author probe | exact program, step labels, expected/observed states, process result, and candidate identity; no inferred state mechanism |
| Artifact basis receipt | Host custody | exact artifact blob, last-changing/source-basis commit, source head, and derivation time; never an editable header's claim of currency |
| Mechanical delta map | Host custody | complete changed commits/paths/versions/hashes between exact heads; no declaration of semantic impact or relevant target section |
| Structural artifact map | Mechanical provider | stable region IDs, headings/symbol titles, exact ranges, hashes, and locators tied to one blob; no semantic ranking or recommended read |
| Addressable-object registry | Mechanical provider | stable ID, kind, authority, version, abstract/tags when mechanically sourced, and locator; known IDs remain directly readable without query admission |
| Active working set | Acting model plus literal provider | exact acquired objects/ranges, cumulative visible bytes, registry/task residency, overlap/reopens, prompt occupancy; never inferred from a per-read cap or selective-read count |
| Local action | Acting model | response schema, basis identities, exact replacement bytes |
| Recomposition | Mechanical applicator first; model integrator only as its own treatment | ordering, overlap, before/after identity, untouched bytes |
| Semantic grade | Precommitted rubric plus direct adjudication | binding to exact candidate and evidence used |

Custody must not silently promote a model-authored binding or obligation into
truth. A mechanically exact wrong map remains wrong.
